text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up I have been enjoying this as a solo game but am happy that it won't be hard to teach friends.

Unlike some games there isn't a finite number of turns...the game ends when someone defeats the boss then each players points are tallied. I like that aspect a lot.

There are some "power" type blocks that benefit all players when one player has success with it.

The art is very cool and whimsical. The paper is sufficient but not very heavy duty. You get plenty of maps...there are 4 of each distinct map design. It's a busy map and I plan on taking the cheapest route possible and using regular sheet protectors and dry erase markers.

I'm not liking the wooden dice at all. For the money I would have really liked some fancier dice. Maybe bigger...maybe more colorful.
You get 4 short presharpened pencils that ...don't have erasers and your first game or two you might need to correct something.

Basically this could have been a print and play. There's nothing at all spectacular about the contents.

My personal little gripe is I don't see how you can be in two places at once. You can attack the map from different sides of the map moving in from starter sections.

That's seems like a lot of negativity but it is a fun little game anyway. You can play it on a small table or most places since there aren't components other than a map and the dice. Also this can encourage people to play who maybe aren't that into games since you don't unload tons of intimidating cards, counters and pieces.

It's a very fine experience. It could've been better for the money though.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up

Ben Franklin Toys Electronic Bill & Coin Counter Bank with LCD Screen, One Size This was a great idea, that totally failed.
The idea is good - you push coins through the slot, and it counts them. You want to add notes, fold them up, push them through the note slot, and press the button representing the value of the note. This is clever, as identifying notes is pretty expensive tech, and the buttons are easy enough to use.
If you push the coins through too quickly, they dont get counted - you have to push them as slowly as you can and even then it has a tenancy to thing quarters are pennys.
The reset button is unusually deep, it was easier to take the batteries out. Then, as you screw the lid back on, make sure you dont press one of the buttons, or you will be repeating the process.
Want to know how much money you have (assuming it counted it correctly?) to do this you have to add more money! There is no way to get it to tell you whats in it without adding to it.
It could be a lot of fun, and practical. Sadly its annoying and useless.

The irregular shape of the pieces, the non-standard design, the pieces that do not snap together, and the heavier pieces were stress-inducing. The pleasure of solving a puzzle was replaced with a difficult challenge that was too much work to enjoy.

If the person solving this puzzle is more up for a challenge, then this might be ok. If the person is older, does not like things that are different, has anxiety, and does not like challenges, then this would not be a good gift.

The difficulty level is high even though the number of pieces is low. This puzzle is not suitable for kids.

The price is much higher than a typical puzzle. The higher price point is understandable based on the quality, but it does not translate to a more enjoyable activity when solving this. Being 5x the price of a regular puzzle does not translate to 5x the level of enjoyment. At the higher price, this would be something to buy as a gift for someone, just be careful of who you give it to.
text_fidelity_b: LEOGOR XL Whimsical Wooden Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults with Shaped Animal Pieces (Lion Puzzle - 339 pcs - 19.7" x 12.4" in) - Laser Cut and Challenging for a Unique Puzzle Experience

Nature Bound Ant Treehouse Habitat Kit with Sand, Connector Tube, Feeding Stick & Insect Instructions, One Size This ant home(tree house) is much smaller than I was expecting, but it's not tiny. Make sure you look at the measurements, though, so your little ones aren't disappointed.

This comes with great directions, so you're led through what you need to do. You can order ants, but the directions are clear for if you chose to collect your own. The kit comes with a coupon to get cheaper ants. (I can't imagine anyone wanting ants bad enough to pay almost $20 for them.) The coupon and the first order page on the website says you'll get 5-10 ants, but then the main page says 30. Even with the coupon code, you're still paying $9.95 for ants(shipping IS included in that price). I can't pay that much when ants are in such abundance around our home. Again, though, I DO give them credit for the great directions for just using ants from the yard. You aren't expected to buy the ants, but you do have that option. Also, to make it clear, you won't get a queen ant if you order. You'll only get non-reproductive ants. (That information is from the website page for ordering the ants.)

It only took my boys a few minutes to come running with more than enough ants to fill their new little home. Unfortunately, our ants have been very slow to feel at home. One died, though we followed directions exactly. They aren't working together like I thought they would, either. That said, so far it has been greatly exciting to watch what little they have done. One ant looks like Goliath upside the other ants, so he's been easier to watch. It's surprisingly fascinating to watch ants move sand around! I assume there will be more efforts from the other ants with time, but I was expecting quicker results. (I don't blame that on the ant farm, by any means!)

One other complaint is the fact that the bottom goes on so loosely. I kept working with it thinking it should be tighter, but had no luck. This is something that will be best watched without too much handling from children, since there are 4 pieces that are easily removed. This kit comes with a tube, which can connect to another tree house if you chose to buy more. (The 2 side pieces can be removed for this connection.)

Overall, this is a fun kit for kids, but it could have been better designed. Every child needs to have the joy of watching ants work, though! ;)

Advantus 12 Inch Desktop World Globe with Blue Oceans (30502),13 W x 12 D x 15 H in Does a perfect globe exist? Probably it does, but I couldn’t afford it. I’m happy with this one although it isn’t perfect.
The good stuff: it came in a super sturdy box that held the globe stable during transport. (The manufacturer ships it, not Amazon.) The stand seems strong and sturdy, and of course I’m grateful for the 720° rotation. The colors are attractive. I even like the raised texture where there are mountain ranges. I’m glad that the United States is divided into states. Finally, although I’m not 100% educated on geography, I can say this globe is up-to-date enough for my purposes; for example, Sudan is divided into Sudan and South Sudan.
The less-good stuff: I’m surprised to see that Canada’s provinces are named, but not outlined! Unless the lines are just so fine that I can’t see them, you have to guess their boundaries. Some cities are identified in the US states, but I was really surprised to see that state capitals are not identified! I suppose some state capitals are named, but Austin Texas (where we live), Tallahassee Florida, and other states I’m familiar with have various cities but not their capitals identified! I also think that city placement is close, but not 100% accurate. Nevertheless, this globe will get a lot of use in homeschooling, and will serve our purposes. I would buy the same globe again if I needed to for some reason.
text_fidelity_b: Advantus 12 Inch Desktop World Globe with Blue Oceans (30502),13 W x 12 D x 15 H in

text_fidelity_a:
Loopdedoo – DIY Friendship Bracelet Maker Kit – Make Bracelets in Minutes – Award-Winning Craft Kit - Ages 8+ It's suggested for ages 8 and older, and I'd agree with that age range. I think younger kids could successfully use it if an older, experience person was nearby to help. Basically, you loop embroidery thread around the two hooks to create the desired core thickness, then twist a knob to spin the core while you lay down an outer design over that core. You tie on the finished piece using the end loops. The bracelet should withstand normal wear if tied according to the directions.

The distance from one hook to the other is 11", but longer items can be made by linking finished 11" pieces or by a somewhat trickier shifting of the piece after you have 11" of it's length finished. You can, of course, make lengths shorter than 11". The instructional book was easy to follow and was all I needed to create a nice bracelet with no frustration involved. They also have good instructional videos on their website: annwilliamsgroup. com/instructional-videos

Included in the kit is the main Loopdedoo tool (with a push-out drawer for storing the thread and clips); instructional booklet; 18 skeins of embroidery thread (100% cotton, 8.7 yards) in a variety of colors including reds through purples, black, brown, and cream; and 2 alligator clips (which are used with the tool to hold threads in place when making the longer items). The thread is Made in China, but I think the loop Loopdedoo is made in the USA.

I hope to use this tool with a group of middle grade girls soon as I think they'll get a kick out of it. The Loopdedoo is made from a solid plastic that feels like it will last. Is this fairly simplistic tool worth price? Well, if the person it's intended for will only make a few bracelets and then move on to the next toy, then probably not. But if she loves to make her own, unique bracelets and tends to continue with an activity she enjoys, then this might be a good tool to support her creativity.
text_fidelity_b: Loopdedoo – DIY Friendship Bracelet Maker Kit – Make Bracelets in Minutes – Award-Winning Craft Kit - Ages 8+

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Kanoodle Jr. Brain Boosting Puzzle Game, Brain Teaser Game for Kids Teens, & Adults, 2-D & 3-D Puzzles, Great For Travel, Gift For Kids Ages 4 to 7 What a great puzzle. Kanoodle is a one-player game in which you take 6 tetris-like pieces and use them to fill in a pattern on the square board. There are 60 puzzles in this group, all included in a book form. I do have a few minor issues, enough to remove one star:

- The puzzles are delivered in the form of a book. There are multiple languages of instructions inside, then you get to the puzzles. Each puzzle is well-done, but the book itself is not the ideal way of presenting the puzzles. Since you're either balancing the book on the shelf above the board, or pulling it out or putting it back underneath the board, it gets scuffed, torn and bent up rather quickly. On day 3, our book looks like a mess. It should have been thicker cards with a separate rulebook.

- Some kids will master this quickly. My four-year-old is on 4-star puzzles already, and we've owned the game for less than 3 days. I think she'll be stuck here for a decent while, and she does enjoy going back to re-do easier puzzles, but I think she's got the hang of it quickly. Yesterday, she completed puzzle 43 out of 60, and they're ordered by difficulty.

This review may sound negative, but let me emphasize that THIS IS SUCH A GOOD TOY! You can see the wheels turning in my daughter's brain as she tries to figure out how to make it work. If you're going on a road trip, this is a must.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Kanoodle Jr. Brain Boosting Puzzle Game, Brain Teaser Game for Kids Teens, & Adults, 2-D & 3-D Puzzles, Great For Travel, Gift For Kids Ages 4 to 7

Would be neat if they could have figured out a way to make it fold up like a case - similar to the way the old Barbie Friend Ship (airplane) did. There's not much as far as assembly goes. (Just snapping 3 pieces together, and then attaching the whole building into that.) It only took a minute or so.

Elmo is detached from the rest of the set, and he holds onto a hand "lens". Letters are hidden throughout the building, on both sides. You can tell where a letter is going to be...circle with squiggly lines. You can't tell what letter it is until Elmo's "lens" is held over it, though. To find some of the letters, the child will have to turn a couple of wheels, and lift the trash can lid, but most of them are in plain view.

This is a fun little toy for learning letters. It doesn't take up a ton of room, either. It's somewhat flat in design, so it could easily slide into a little nook somewhere, and just pull it out for learning time. I think most children will tire quickly of it if they have full access to it, unless they have other Sesame Street toys(or something else similar) that could be used with it, apart from just hunting for letters. I think it's probably better for special times, though, for most children. There's really not a great deal to it, but it is fun and neat.

text_fidelity_a:
Arizona GameCo Smack it! Card Game for Kids | Ages 6-12 | Fun, Fast-paced and Easy to Learn | Family Game Night Friendly | a Great Boy or Girl Gift Idea Fairly fun game but card quality is poor for the price. I doubt this is a game to play for hours on end yet.....at the price point I would appreciate brand playing card quality. Is the game bad? I have "dealt" with worse.....there are certainly other card games....even Uno; cheaper, with better card quality but after all....this is a fast slap game. The cards feel cheap, look cheap and shuffle the same. They shuffle in a manegable way but to me this is almost disposable card stock quality. The "art" is non existent with numbers simple written and spelled on the card...colors also do not matter.
Your kids might just toss them on the table and mish mosh them to shuffle them. That will work fine. Slamwich has the excellent card quality and is also a fast easy slap game along this price point. If I had a re-do, I would just stick with Slamwich. Card stock is higher quality and game itself is a little more in depth and kids and adults enjoy a few rounds.

I cannot in good conscience recommend this at 8 dollars or higher. The gameplay itself is simple old fashioned war with a light/slight twist. Number cards....say a 14 verus a 32 dont matter at all (the 32 doesnt take the pile)....it is all about the "slap cards" and "challenege cards"...challenge is where your higher number card played actually counts for once. I DO see that very young kids would enjoy it. I do not see this being a "drinking game" or fun for adults without some extra house rules. Quality is simply subpar for the price. The business is in the USA, the cards and actual game itself are outsourced to China if that matters to you.

Rating is ....average. These are close or are average card size....they have a slick coat. The plain white background quickly picks up color bleed or whatever.....

It is not horrible but just eeks in at "ok" for simple card games. It isnt great and it isnt a big go to except for maybe the 7 year old children set...and the box states...6 plus for age and 2 to 7 people. I say...skip don't smack.
text_fidelity_b: Arizona GameCo Smack it! Card Game for Kids | Ages 6-12 | Fun, Fast-paced and Easy to Learn | Family Game Night Friendly | a Great Boy or Girl Gift Idea

text_fidelity_a:
B. Toys by Battat B. Jungle Jam - Toy Drum Set (Includes 9 Percussion Instruments for Kids) (BX1289Z) The leopard-faced conga drum is about 15" tall and 10" wide. The drum barrel has handles on each side for easy lifting (though everything is very light). The lid has ten large bells on it, and it can be removed from the drum and used as a tambourine. Stored inside are two snakes (drumsticks), two giraffes (maracas/rattles), a hornbill (water whistle--you fill with water in the hole in the head, then blow on the whistle for a warble sound), an antelope (slide whistle--you blow in the whistle while sliding the legs in and out to change the tone), and a crocodile (cabasa-clacker--you rotate the handle to make the drum play itself).

It's supposed to be for ages 2-6. My just-turned-1-year-old niece loves playing with this, and so do the adults. The only thing my niece couldn't figure out yet were the whistles. (The water whistle requires just the right amount of water and blowing angle to warble, otherwise it'll do a high pitched whistle.) Our house has become full of joyful noise. lol. Anyway, this set looks fairly sturdy and has been holding up to play just fine so far, but it's clearly a kids-level quality in terms of the sound.
text_fidelity_b: B. Toys by Battat B. Jungle Jam - Toy Drum Set (Includes 9 Percussion Instruments for Kids) (BX1289Z)

Giant Delta Kite 6 x 7.5 ft Easy Flyer with String and Handle, Classic Delta Kite, Brilliant Colors in The Sky What a great kite. This thing took off easy, flew all day and looked great. I had read some of the reviews about the tails tattering in the wind so I took a proactive approach. As soon as I received it I opened it and inspected.... all looked good. The other reviewers suggested putting tape on the ends of the tails...I got a bottle of good old fashioned Elmers white glue and rubbed it on both sides of the end of the tails..about 2 or 3 inches up and let it dry. Well got to the beach and let her go....after a full day sun and fun, I reeled it in and zero tattering on the ends, however there was some unraveling in random spot on the rest of the tails...so maybe next time I will apply the glue up each side.
I would like to add that as far as the string goes, I went to the local wally store and in the fishing section I found about 300 feet of bright yellow nylon cord (used for catfish) about 2 bucks and a reel right next to it for about 2 bucks, Made the task of reeling it in much easier than the supplied equipment....buy it...you will have a good time.

That car goes fairly slowly.  This thing flies and is NOT a toddler toy.  There's no way I'm putting the remote control in the hands an 18 mos. old, even as smart as he is!  The remote offers very little control and that's risky when you have something moving that fast around the floor.  The car doesn't stay on a straight path either.  While moving forward it veers left and right at random and moving backwards is crazy.  The colors are vibrant enough to get a child's attention.  The buttons you push to play sounds are easy to work.  Those are the steering wheel, the driver, and the top of the car.  Pressing the steering wheel causes the cute sound of a car cranking, revving its engine, and rumbling while idle.  The top button causes the weirdest, most random song I've ever heard on a child's toy and it goes on for a solid 36.40 seconds.  Yes, I timed it for this review.  It's that weird a song. When the driver is pressed, the car emits an odd vocalization that sounds like a cross between a dog barking and a man shouting "hey! Hey hey hey! Heeey!" (like something one might hear at the end of a nice Latin dance song) in an odd singsong voice.  The headlights flash whenever a button is pushed and do so for the entirety of whatever sound is playing.  The driver is detachable and once it's pressed down well, it takes some force to get it out.  The overall look of the car and remote is cute, like any regular toddler toy should be.  For an older child who knows how to handle a faster paced remote control car, the price is fair.  As a so called toddler toy...no way am I putting this anywhere near a small child.
text_fidelity_b: KINGBOT DeXop Rc Cartoon Car Cartoon Race Car with Music Radio Control Toy Action Figure Rc Vehicle for Toddler, CR04

Takenoko Board Game | Bamboo Farming Game | Panda Themed Strategy Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 8+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Matagot We had the pleasure of playing this in our most recent game night, and it was delightful. You start with a few "quests" based on bamboo for pandas to eat, bamboo in the "fields", and the arrangement of those "field" tiles (as well as access to water ...). It's actually rather simple. Each turn you get to expand the game by adding field tiles (up adding water or other upgrades to the tiles), grow bamboo, have the panda eat the bamboo, or take on more "quests". As everything but the bamboo the panda eats belongs to everyone, there's a passive cooperation, and other than the score at the end (based on completing those cards), it doesn't feel that competitive. If another player lays down irrigation, that's not irrigation that solely benefits them or takes away from what you have, rather it adds to what you have and may well help complete one of your quests. We played with folks from 7 years old on up, and everyone had a great time.

The only real negative (and I don't see the need to deduct any stars from the rating) is that this is at max a four player game. I could'd imagine playing with less than 3, and 4 really is the sweet spot.

text_fidelity_a:
ThinkFun Zingo Sight Words Award Winning Early Reading Game for Pre-K to 2nd Grade - Toy of the Year Finalist, A Fun and Educational Game Developed by Educators for Boys and Girls, Multicolor My boys are 3, 5, and 7(almost 8), and they all enjoy this game. As a bonus, it requires NO batteries!

Both the game boards and the game pieces have both pictures and words on them. Your child doesn't have to be able to read to play the game, but it does make the picture/word connection, to an extent. The game goes so fast that even I tend to mostly just look at the picture, and ignore the words. There is still a slight connection, though, and every little bit helps when a little one is learning words.

The game comes with 7 game boards. These are double sided. The green side is for a less competitive game, and better for the littlest ones. There aren't that many shared pictures on this side, and the players aren't in so much of a rush to grab the tiles. The red side has a bit more competition, since there are more pictures in common. The players have to rush to grab a matching tile, before someone else grabs it.

Each game goes really quick, so you're not spending a ton of time on each game. There are a few different options for playing the game. You can go the traditional "Bingo" route, or you can match designs, play multiple cards, or even fill up the whole card, which is what my oldest prefers. The traditional route is just way too quick for my children's tastes.

Their favorite part of the game is the Zinger. It's super easy to load the tiles, and then slide them into view. They have to take turns sliding the tiles into view, because it's so much fun. The only negative we've seen is the fact that sometimes it seems the same tile is being played over and over(in a row). When you first open the box, you'll have to mix these tiles up, since they are placed together matched. If you don't mix them up, you WILL have the same tile continue to show up in a row. Even then, it sometimes happens that the same one will keep showing up. It is easy to dump them out, mix them up, and then reload them, though.

This is a super simple game, but so much fun for little ones! I even enjoy playing it with them, which is pretty important.
text_fidelity_b: ThinkFun Zingo Sight Words Award Winning Early Reading Game for Pre-K to 2nd Grade - Toy of the Year Finalist, A Fun and Educational Game Developed by Educators for Boys and Girls, Multicolor

The 1,100 piece kit from Building Bricks was exactly what we were looking for. The Big Questions:
1. Do they really work well with Lego Brand Legos?
Yes - they work very well. It's difficult to tell the difference if you're not really trying hard.
2. How much cheaper are they? Is it really worth it?
It's hard to compare exact pricing here because this set does not include wheels, doors or special pieces. If I had to choose a product to compare it to, I'd probably compare it with Lego's XXL Classic Box (https://www.amazon.com/10697-Building-Large-Creator-Pieces/dp/B00XJ5C4FW). When pricing per piece, the Lego box is about 5¢ per piece. And yes, you read that right. You're dolling out a nickel for every piece of plastic with Lego's brand stamped on it. :) Building Bricks runs about 3¢ per piece. So the answer is: It's almost half the price - very worth it if you're just needing a lot of standard pieces.
As a side note: We really liked the color choices Building Bricks made. They're perfect for expanding your Lego creation palette.

Thames & Kosmos Word Slam Family | Fast-Paced Multiplayer Party Card & Word Game | High Playercount | Based On The Award Winning Word Slam Word Slam Family is a nice game that's easy to play, despite the dense rule sheet that comes with the game. You can set this up and play it quickly, and it's easy enough that it truly is a family weight game. You don't even need to be a reader to get some of the clues, assuming an adult is there to help.

That said, this game is a very straightforward, and less interesting game than the hundreds that are just like it, but with a twist (Decrypto, Codenames, Funglish, Crosstalk, Insider, Werewords, When I Dream, etc). It's a one-word for one-word style association game, that, quite frankly, is done better by most of it's competitors. I think that this one might appeal to those who really like the small box size, or who haven't played any competitors, but as someone who has, this adds nothing new to the genre, and does not have the staying power of it's rivals.

eeBoo French Flash Cards I had the great fortune of parents who made sure I learned three other languages as a kid. They started very early with me and I distinctly remember them making their own flashcards. It's too bad that they didn't have access to these beautiful, affordable, and very easy to use flashcards to aid them! Now, as a parent, teacher, and a nanny, I work hard to teach my kids the basics of French and Spanish, and I stumbled across these. They have been well worth the price and they were highly affordable. Best of all, my kids that I teach love the cards and enjoy using them too. I would recommend them to both the beginner and the advanced speaker as they embark on teaching others.

There are a few times that the cards use outdated pronunciations or word choices, but it's actually a plus in my book because it aids further in teaching. When I see a card with a different context of pronunciation or word choice than what is currently popular or commonly used, then I can supplement by saying "Or you could say it like this ..." Anyways, the cards are really lovely and sturdy. They seem sort of indestructible because one of the kids I nanny is 18 months old and a total "rip things to shreds" sort and he wasn't even able to destroy one! They also wipe off nicely with a damp cloth.

Do consider using these for your own kids! You wont be sorry!

text_fidelity_a:
The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure This is a 'cute' little toy. I like the expression on his face. We've had fun playing with it for the past couple weeks.

Some things that you might want to know about it if you're considering buying one.

The instructions suggest replacing the two AAA batteries when you take the figure out of the package - the two that come in it are for 'in-store' demonstration purposes. Opening the battery compartment I found that the supplied batteries are pretty decent alkaline ones. Still, I replaced the ones in mine as I hate it when batteries go dead in a device and then leak. Something to maybe mention - the battery compartment is secured with a screw, so that small hands can't get into it.

The tail on the rabbit acts as the on/off switch. There are three setting - On, Off, and Demo. In the demonstration mode the figure talks and the wheels turn for a few seconds and then stops. When in the On position, the figure says a phrase - the wheels go for awhile and then it stops and repeats the cycle. The figure has three wheels - two fixed wheels seem to drive it's motion and a third rotates to make the figure go in different directions. Our rabbit seems to have a habit of finding the nearest corner and parking itself in it. The figure's eyes move a bit when it's in running around (although it's hard to see with the way it's eyes are set).

The figure comes with a separate carrot prop. Which the rabbit is suppose to hold in it's one hand - ours kept dropping his. So I took a piece of the white string that had secured the toy to the package and tied the carrot to his hand- you can't really even see it.

The rabbit talks, and I know it's suppose to be Kevin Hart doing a 'cartoon' voice - but it's really hard to understand what it's suppose to be saying. Hopefully when the movie comes out the phrases will be more recognizable.

All in all I like this figure and I'm looking forward to seeing the movie.
text_fidelity_b: The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure

text_fidelity_a:
WowWee - MiP the Toy Robot - White This is a four star product in many ways. But I'm giving it three due to the following factors...

Excellent build quality and hardware features. However, without some additional software and accessories this you won't see lasting use.

Hardware: you WILL need a phone or tablet to unlock the limited potential of this toy. The included gesture and sound functionality is too rudimentary (and yet also hard to acess consistently) for lasting interest. If you don't plan to provide access to a tablet or phone, get WowWee's robotic dog product instead. Although it is easy to set up an obstacle course or seesaw on your own, purpose-built accessories would go a long way towards providing a "fiction" for the toy to inhabit, as well as proven fun activities.

Software: the existing apps are very well made and provide a significant boost to the toys functionality. I'd say about 75%. However, most are of limited scope and soon become repetitive. The best feature is the ability to remotely drive the robot and also record its adventures. I'd like to see a feature that allows kids to rudimentarily program the robot (perhaps to interact with purpose built accessories) not just activate sounds and colored lights... I'd also like to see the toolset opened to adults (Lua scripting?) so that they can extend the functionality for Pre-K through K STEM learning.

I understand trying to hit price points is important. But this is either a $75 toy with a few $25 accessory kits, or a $125 toy all in. The existing package (while decent) is limiting the potential of the product.
text_fidelity_b: WowWee - MiP the Toy Robot - White

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Labyrinth Family Board Game for Kids and Adults Age 7 and Up - Millions Sold, Easy to Learn and Play with Great Replay Value (26448) So....I'm Gen X and we played the original version some in college along with games like Risk and Stratego on weekends. It isnt quite a fluff game but it isnt very hard. I would think both children and adults would enjoy this game. A game adults can enjoy with their kids....or a fun starter game or game for chatting and having a beverage or three.

The best part is there is hardly any explanation needed to get started. Move tiles to open a path to get to the objects on your cards. And....block others from their goals. I love this game especially with 3 or 4 people instead of two. It requires some strategy but luck can make or break it, too.

Harry Potter version! Yes! Well...it is beautiful. The board looks wonderful! But in this version you are gathering "people" or characters rather than treasure items. The premise makes sense. Going through the maze that is Hogwarts gathering people ....you must match cards in your hands to pics on the tiles of the gameboard. Sounds AWESOME. In reality...it is kind of messy because some people look similar. Some people are the big characters...such as Harry or Snape....there were 3 I was like....who on earth is THIS and I thought I was a big fan. So....due to the pics on the game board being rather small....they are also color coded too. If your card is Harry with a blue border....Harry has a blue border on the game tile as well. But is there another character who looks very similar on the board with a blue border? Yes there is. So....yeah, it is really cool BUT pay good attention as the character pictures certainly are NOT as easy to discern as a scarab or diamond in the original. Hey...but it looks great!

I give this game 10 out of 10 because my gripes do not effect the game. If you are are a HP fan....and you already like or think you might like a labyrinth game...here ya go. This is 100% Ravensburg quality. The box is good quality as all the pieces. The box holds everything in the usual labyrinth organized way. Very nice.

At the price point....I really, really, really dont like wooden pegs. They are sort of big, bright and easy to move but I liked the Labyrinth version with the plastic characters NOT the one with wooden pegs. I have no idea WHY if your player piece coincides with a house....such as Slytherin....they didnt atleast make little plastic coats of armor for each house. I just hate generic pegs in fun games. But it doesnt make the game any better or worse. I saw some reviews where people complained about the card quality. It is the same it always has been. The cards are simply there to identify your next goal. This game doesnt require shuffling like Uno or slapping...or grabbing or swapping cards. They are perfectly fine.

Great game. Great Ravensburger quality. Dear Ravensburger.....I sure would love a Scooby Doo version with cool plastic player pieces!

I included pics and pics of game pieces from an earlier version of the original game
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Labyrinth Family Board Game for Kids and Adults Age 7 and Up - Millions Sold, Easy to Learn and Play with Great Replay Value (26448)
